documents.title: AI Resources (incl. Generative AI Guidance for Privacy and Security)
documents.summary: IT Services page on AI risks, built-in AI tools in BGSU software, and tools for detecting or preventing student AI use. Mostly privacy and security advice for staff and students; it says student AI use on coursework is 'not ideal' but sets no rule.
documents.stance_why: The ITS page sets no classroom rule and mostly gives privacy and security cautions; it says student use for assignments 'is not ideal' and points to CFE for teaching, leaving course-level decisions open, so delegates.

units.why: Requires formal review before any new AI tool is adopted: 'are required for implementation of any new AI tool for university use'. Institutional set-up, binds departments; P50 (vetted tools) fits better than P65 because it is a technology-review gate, not a contract/data-sharing rule.
units.anchor: are required for implementation of any new AI tool for university use
units.frag_start: Formal project requests and technology reviews
units.frag_end: any new AI tool for university use.

units.why: The user or department must keep BGSU-specific data accurate: 'is responsible for making sure the data is in place, accurate, and maintained'. It is an accountability rule for AI output quality, so P31 rather than P29 (which concerns student submissions).

units.frag_start: If an AI tool is expected to provide BGSU-specific data/results

units.why: Defines AI by quoting TechTarget: 'the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines'. A definition that sets what the page covers, so P61 and 'informs'.

documents.title: AI Literacy: Academic Honesty & Citation
documents.summary: Library guide page on citing AI and academic honesty. It sends students to their syllabus or instructor, defines misconduct terms, asks for citation, and advises instructors to state AI rules and be wary of detectors.
documents.stance_why: The guide says 'there are no campus-wide policies' and tells students to 'ask your instructor about their individual policy', handing the decision to instructors, so delegates.
